issue.title: macros.md %wait row omits the for_epic follow default and for_epic=false opt-out
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1h7.10 note #1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP), triaged by the sase-1h7 land agent.

The `%wait` row in `sase/memory/macros.md` (the directive table) still reads
"Dependency; bare = last named; `%wait(time=5m)` / `#t:5m` time floor". Since sase-1h7.10
(c7190fb99a), `WAIT_FOR_EPIC_DEFAULT` is true: a wait on a user-authored agent target
also follows every epic that target (or any member of its session, clan, workflow, or
bound tribe) launches, until those epic beads close. `%wait(<target>, for_epic=false)`
opts out. `for_epic=` needs an agent target in the same occurrence (hard error otherwise),
`<base>--plan` targets never follow, and `sase bead work` emits `for_epic=false` for
intra-epic phase and land sequencing waits. Agents reading only the memory row will
mis-predict when a `%wait:planner` releases.

The user-facing docs (`docs/macros.md`, `docs/axe.md`, `docs/beads.md`) were updated by
the flip phase. Only the memory note is stale, and memory edits need explicit user
approval, so the epic left it alone.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Extend the %wait row (or the %wait paragraph after the table) to say agent targets follow every epic the target launches until those epics close (for_epic=true default); %wait(target, for_epic=false) opts out; for_epic= needs an agent target; --plan rows never follow; sase bead work emits for_epic=false for phase sequencing.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1h7.10 flipped %wait to follow launched epics by default; the core macros memory row still describes the old release semantics and memory edits were out of the epic's scope.
